payload.comment: The comparison stage is internally consistent and arithmetically correct. Verification: (1) accuracy_delta = 0.887883 − 0.821309 = 0.066574 ✓; (2) baseline_met_or_exceeded = true since 0.887883 > 0.821309 ✓; (3) common_seed (42) matches both baseline_report.seed and the agentic run's seed ✓; (4) common_split_fingerprint (9afc9ed3…) is identical in both reports, confirming a fair same-split comparison ✓; (5) agentic_accuracy (0.887883) matches evaluation_report.accuracy ✓; (6) baseline_accuracy (0.821309) matches baseline_report.accuracy ✓; (7) both use the same dataset (pathmnist) and same epoch budget (15) ✓. The baseline is a fixed tiny_cnn (depth 2, hidden 16, no class weighting, no dropout) serving as a conventional control, which is a reasonable comparison setup. The agentic model (res_cnn_wider_deep, selected via 4-trial search) achieves a +6.66 pp accuracy improvement and a +10.46 pp macro-F1 improvement (0.8555 vs 0.7509), both meaningful gains. Minor observations (not errors): the comparison_report only surfaces the primary metric (accuracy) and does not explicitly include macro_f1_delta, balanced_accuracy_delta, or per-class deltas; no statistical significance test (e.g., paired bootstrap or McNemar) is reported on the 7,180-sample test set, though the magnitude of the delta makes significance near-certain; the comparison does not decompose the improvement by class to show whether gains are uniform or concentrated in previously weak classes (e.g., cancer-associated stroma, smooth muscle). These are scope limitations of the comparison artefact rather than correctness issues. No deterministic findings were raised. The comparison is valid, fair, and correctly computed.
llm_issues: Comparison report omits macro_f1_delta (0.855476 vs 0.750857 = +0.104619) and balanced_accuracy_delta, limiting the multi-metric picture to a single primary metric
No statistical significance test (e.g., paired bootstrap CI or McNemar test) reported on the 7,180-sample test set to formally confirm the 6.66 pp accuracy delta is non-random
No per-class delta decomposition provided to show whether the improvement is uniform or concentrated in specific classes (e.g., cancer-associated stroma F1 0.647, smooth muscle F1 0.705)
